name: North America
blurb: Prairie, boreal forest and two long coasts: plowed grasslands, huge fires, a river mouth starved of oxygen, pines killed by a non-native fungus and whales that share their sea with ships and gear.

issues.title: The Vanishing Prairie

drivers.name: Conversion to row crops (wheat, corn, soy)
Roads, wells and wind and oil development

fact.text: WWF’s 2024 Plowprint report estimated that 1.9 million acres of grassland in the US and Canadian Great Plains were converted to cropland in 2022, an improvement on the previous ten-year average of 2.6 million acres a year; about 55% of the Plains’ grassland remains intact.
fact.source: World Wildlife Fund, Plowprint Report 2024 (press release, 26 September 2024)

also.source: Food and Environment Reporting Network, “Grassland losses slow in Great Plains”

issues.realWorld: Choose beef from ranchers who keep native grass, support land trusts that buy conservation easements, and ask what your local farm bill does for grassland.

issues.title: The Boreal Fire Season

drivers.name: Fuel and ignitions at the forest edge

sites: A community on the forest edge

fact.text: Natural Resources Canada says that in 2023 over 6,800 wildland fires burned more than 14.6 million hectares of Canada’s forest area, roughly seven times the typical annual area, compared with an average of more than 2.1 million hectares in an ordinary year.

issues.realWorld: Follow fire bans and smoke advisories, prepare your own evacuation plan if you live near forest, and support groups that restore burned habitat.

issues.title: Lights Out for Migrants
sites: A coastal city on a flyway
A forest stopover in the suburbs

fact.text: A 2017 study in PNAS found that New York’s Tribute in Light installation altered the behaviour of an estimated 1.1 million migrating birds over seven nights across seven years, making them gather in high densities, slow down and circle; the disruption disappeared when the lights were switched off.
fact.source: Van Doren et al., PNAS (2017), “High-intensity urban light installation dramatically alters nocturnal bird migration”

also.source: Audubon, “How to bring Lights Out to a city near you” (18 March 2022)

issues.realWorld: Turn off or shield outdoor lights at night in spring and autumn, close blinds in tall buildings, and ask building owners to join a Lights Out programme.

issues.title: The Whitebark Pine

drivers.name: The introduced rust fungus Cronartium ribicola

sites: A burned slope waiting for replanting

fact.text: The US Fish and Wildlife Service listed whitebark pine as a threatened species on 14 December 2022, saying white pine blister rust, a non-native fungal disease, remains the primary threat and that, as of 2016, an estimated 51% of all standing whitebark pine trees are dead.
fact.source: US Fish and Wildlife Service press release (December 2022)

issues.realWorld: Stay on trails and report dead or dying high-elevation pines to the land agency, and support groups that collect seed from rust-resistant trees.

issues.title: The Gulf’s Dead Zone

drivers.name: Drained wetlands that no longer filter water

sites: A shrimp and crab fishing ground

fact.text: NOAA-supported scientists measured the 2026 Gulf dead zone at about 1,332 square miles, one of the smallest on record; excess nutrients from the Mississippi-Atchafalaya River Basin drive it, and the Hypoxia Task Force aims to cut the five-year average to under 1,900 square miles by 2035.
fact.source: NOAA-supported scientists’ announcement (5 August 2026), via the Gulf Hypoxia monitoring project

also.source: NOAA National Centers for Coastal Ocean Science (31 July 2025), on the dead-zone target

issues.realWorld: Use less fertiliser on lawns and gardens, buy from farms that use cover crops and buffer strips, and support groups restoring wetlands along rivers.

issues.title: Right Whales and Ropes
sites: The Cape Cod Bay feeding ground

fact.text: NOAA Fisheries estimated 384 individual North Atlantic right whales at the start of 2024 (an October 2025 update, with a margin of +10/-9), and names entanglement in fishing gear and vessel strikes as the leading causes of North Atlantic right whale mortality.
fact.source: NOAA Fisheries, North Atlantic right whale species page

issues.realWorld: Choose seafood from fisheries using whale-safe, ropeless or weak-rope gear, keep to speed limits when boating in slow zones, and report whale sightings.

issues.title: The Kelp that Vanished

fact.text: A peer-reviewed study found that bull kelp forests suffered unprecedented losses along 350 km of coastline in northern California from 2014 through 2019; the shift was initiated by a multi-year marine heatwave, after a sea star wasting epidemic that began in 2013 sharply reduced several sea star species, including the sunflower star.
fact.source: Peer-reviewed study on northern California bull kelp, via PubMed Central

issues.realWorld: Choose sustainable seafood, keep your own emissions down, and support kelp-restoration and sea-star recovery projects along the Pacific coast.
